review_type: Anonymous read-only visual and brand-fit review for professional design-studio case-study readers

method.images: Every supplied A and B capture was viewed individually with native view_image at original detail; no image edits, source inspection or live interaction.
method.scores: Category scores are holistic presentation judgments, not counts of findings.

A.assessment: Software/product-oriented content is present, but all supplied captures present largely default browser HTML. The artifact does not visually demonstrate the studio interface-design quality in the frozen reference.

required_capture_observations.observation: White canvas, default serif body/headings, blue underlined branding/skip links and native small buttons occur consistently. Default presentation is not the intentional near-black, silver, restrained-border studio identity. Labels and values run together, reducing scanning clarity.

Brief content accurately describes responsive commerce, checkout, catalogue/inventory APIs and frontend/backend work. Selected-project information appears before tab content. However investment, progress, revision and next-milestone summaries are visually concatenated, and desktop layout leaves most width unstructured. Mobile wrapping is readable in places but offers little spacing or product-interface hierarchy.

Revision titles and review context exist, but the storefront preview appears as plain text/navigation rather than finished UI artwork. Initial revision/publish captures do not show decision/publish controls; their position outside the viewport alone does not establish absence.

Discussion has an understandable heading, comment and labeled composer. Author/role/date spacing is collapsed, and the narrow default textarea and small native submit control give an unfinished form presentation.

additional_capture_observations.observation: Login contains a clear shared-workspace message and synthetic role selection, but email/password inputs are inline on desktop and awkwardly wrap on mobile; storefront text is not a finished visual preview.

Scrolled discussion capture confirms a visible Post comment control, privacy-context copy and a route to revisions. The form remains a small browser-default textarea/button without deliberate mobile ergonomics.
Scrolled publish capture confirms title, summary and Publish revision 2 controls after existing revision information. Inputs and labels wrap together and lack a clear form layout.

visible_unfinished_assets: All captures visibly lack a composed product style system; storefront/concept artwork is represented by raw text and symbols. The screenshots cannot establish why this occurred.
A.confidence: High for observed visual presentation; medium for workflow readability because some controls/content are outside captured viewports.

B.assessment: A cohesive, credible client/studio product presentation translates the actual dark studio identity into a useful interface. Commerce, merchant-console and SaaS previews tell a software-delivery story rather than a graphic-design-only story.

required_capture_observations.observation: Near-black canvas, pale text, fine borders, serif display headings and muted green state/action accents form a coherent system. Desktop sidebar and summary row are clearly organized. Mobile summary information stacks neatly. Storefront UI preview is composed and merchant/SaaS interface previews are visible on desktop. Mobile project artwork precedes card task details and pushes the Open project control below the first viewport, a modest efficiency tradeoff.

Selected project, status, investment, delivery progress, revision and milestone information are easy to identify; the brief uses a balanced desktop two-column composition and purposeful mobile order. Delivery-progress/current-revision label spacing is overly tight on desktop in this and revision/publish states. Secondary metadata and navigation labels are small.

Revision history is separated from client-review/studio-publication panels on desktop, with clear selected revision context and restrained state badges. Mobile places project information and existing revision ahead of subsequent controls. Initial mobile captures show mainly header/history, so approval controls and complete publish forms need additional scrolled evidence.

Discussion separates prior message and composer clearly, with visible author/role/date context, labeled spacious input and an emphasized Send message action on desktop. The mobile state retains coherent order and readable wrapping; composer lies below the initial viewport.

additional_capture_observations.observation: Desktop login balances a studio headline/product preview with a distinct sign-in panel. Mobile puts the sign-in form before the artwork, with full-width labeled inputs and clear primary action. Synthetic demo account selection is understandable; the full mobile selector list extends beyond the capture.
Scrolled mobile discussion shows a comfortably spaced composer, full-width Send message button and synthetic-information reminder. The form is visually polished and fits the width.

Scrolled mobile publish shows existing revision before selected-publication context, labeled title/summary fields and a clear full-width Publish revision 2 action. Copy explains that publishing opens a fresh review and preserves prior decisions.

visible_unfinished_assets: No broken image, raw placeholder block or visibly unfinished control is apparent in the inspected scope. Product previews are explicitly fictional concept artwork; their miniature embedded text is not intended as the main workflow reading surface.
B.confidence: High for identity, composition and visible form presentation; medium for complete workflow coverage because captures are partial viewports.

limits: Screenshots cannot prove backend correctness, authentication/permissions, persistence, functionality, accessibility conformance or interactivity.
No click, keyboard, focus, hover, validation/error, approval submission, publication outcome or recovery state was tested.
Activity content, complete milestone/deliverable lists, offscreen project cards and client approval action controls are not fully visible in this supplied capture set.
These scores evaluate supplied visible artifacts only; missing styling cause and unseen product scope remain unknown.
The frozen brand text/screenshots provide the sole brand basis. No live-site or historical-score comparison was used.
summary: B is the stronger portfolio presentation and actual AethDesign studio fit in the supplied pixels. A contains relevant software-delivery copy and identifiable workflow controls but appears visually incomplete.
